source_title: 101 Ways To Be a Better Person
attribution: Adapted from 101 Ways To Be a Better Person by Personal Excellence (https://personalexcellence.co/blog/101-ways-to-be-a-better-person/)

items.title: Commit yourself to growth (Be Growth-oriented)
items.body: The more you grow, the better you become. I committed myself to a lifetime of growth back in 2006 (when I discovered my purpose) and I’ve not looked back since.

items.title: Work on your negative traits
items.body: Are there any traits you dislike about yourself? Some traits that I didn’t like about myself in the past include being self-centered, arrogant, selfish, critical, harsh, and hard. Identify them, and then work on them one by one. It can be challenging to overhaul your character at once. On the other hand, if you work on addressing one negative trait at a time, it’s a lot more manageable and achievable.

items.title: Identify your ideal self
items.body: What’s your ideal self like? Picture them in your mind, and then write down all your ideal traits. Then, start living true to your ideal self.

items.title: Find a role model
items.body: Having a role model inspires us and gives us an image of who we can be. People I’m inspired by include Oprah Winfrey, who has done so much in the area of self-help; Chadwick Boseman, who tirelessly spoke up for the black community even leading up to his death; and John Christopher, a master herbalist who healed people using natural remedies and inspired and educated a new generation of herbalists. Who is/are your role model(s), and what do you like about them?

items.title: Be a role model
items.body: When we are role models to others, it pushes us to think carefully about our actions and sets us up to a higher standard. In being a role model, it’s not about making yourself into someone you’re not (see #57: Be Individualistic). It’s about living true to your ideal self (see #3). How can you be an inspirational guide to others? Live by example.

items.title: Be a better child to your parents
items.body: You only have two parents in your life, so appreciate the time you have with them. If your relationship with your parents is non-ideal, it doesn’t mean that everything ends here. I used to have a very poor relationship with my parents until I achieved a resolution in this area recently.
items.related_read: How I Found Peace in My Relationship with My Parents

items.title: Be a better friend to your friends
items.body: I used to be disappointed at how some of my friends weren’t always there for me when I needed them. Then I realized that I should think about how I can be a better friend to my friends first before having such expectations of others. Likewise, for you, think: How can you be a better friend to your friends?
items.related_read: How to Have More Best Friends in Life

items.title: Be a better sibling, if you have siblings
items.body: I have several friends who are the only child and they frequently talk about how they wish they had a brother or sister. If you’re lucky enough to have a brother or sister, treasure them. Spend more time with them; show them care and concern. Look out for them if you need to.

items.title: Be a better partner, if you’re attached
items.body: If you have a girlfriend/wife or boyfriend/husband, think about how you can be a better partner to her/him. When you’re in a relationship, it’s easy to make demands and have expectations about what your partner should do or be. It’s more difficult to take ownership of what you aren’t doing or being yourself. Commit yourself to be a better partner and release your expectations of your partner. Both of you will be happier that way.

items.title: Be a better parent, if you have children
items.body: Many parents have told me that having a child is one of the most amazing things that has ever happened to them. If you have a child or children, think about how you can be a better parent to them. Raising a child is challenging at every stage of the child’s life, with new things to learn and new problems to conquer, but that’s also part of the joy of being a parent.

items.title: Be a better employee, if you work for someone
items.body: Often I hear people complaining about how their companies aren’t giving them enough benefits/wages/support/etc. While this may be true, think about how you can be a better employee. Check if there’s anything more you can do for your manager. See if there are any new projects you can take on. See how you can improve your current performance.

items.title: Be a better manager/leader, if you’re managing others
items.body: Many people leave their jobs because they’re unhappy with their managers. How well you manage your employees can dramatically affect their motivation level and performance. Put their needs before yours and bring the best out of them.

items.title: Be a better member of your community
items.body: What communities are you a part of? Say, interest groups? Recreational clubs? How can you be a more active member of these communities?

items.title: Be a better human to others
items.body: How can you treat the fellow humans around you better? Start treating them this way.

items.title: Be a better being in this world
items.body: How can you make the world a better place? Start doing that today.

items.title: Be Able
items.body: Your skills are like tools in your toolbox — when you equip yourself with more skills, you literally become more able to add value and contribute to others and society.

subitems.title: Learn something new
subitems.body: No matter how much you know, there are always new things to learn. The more you learn, the better you become.

subitems.title: Hone your current skills
subitems.body: Strengthen your current skills. You can never be too good at something — there’s always room to improve. Even the best people in their fields, such as Tiger Woods (Golf), Michael Jordan (Basketball), and Beethoven (Pianist) never stopped honing their craft.

items.title: Be Accepting of differences — be it of people, mindsets, lifestyles, or cultures
items.body: For they add variety and color to our lives. If everyone is the same, life will be bland — monotonous, even.

items.title: Be Flexible
items.body: Have expectations and ideals, but be flexible about them when needed. Not everyone can perform to high expectations and not every situation can happen perfectly. Learn when to be rigid on your ideals and when to be flexible.

subitems.title: Step out of your comfort zone
subitems.body: Are you sticking to the same routines and hiding behind a safety net? Step out and do something you’ve never done before. It’ll broaden your mind and make you a better person.
subitems.related_read: How To Get Out of Your Comfort Zone

subitems.title: Travel
subitems.body: Traveling broadens perspectives and enriches our minds. Between 2011 and 2017, I spent almost 50% of my time traveling and exploring different continents and countries. This helped me gain many insights into different cultures and enriched my perspective of the world.

subitems.title: Always have the best intentions for others
subitems.body: Go for the highest good in everything you do, every decision you make, and every thought you have.

subitems.title: Volunteer (for a cause you believe in)
subitems.body: Not everything has to be measured in money. At PE, I spend hours every day writing the best content and giving it away for free, without asking anything back in return from the readers. With volunteer work, you may be giving your labor for free, but this is time spent that is filled with meaning. Don’t underestimate the difference you can make in others’ lives with just a few hours of work.

subitems.title: Save the environment
subitems.body: Our world is being wasted away, day after day, and modern society is inflicting huge amounts of damage on it with pollution, plastic waste, and more. What can you do to protect our home?

items.title: Be Assertive
items.body: Stand up for your rights and the things you believe in.

items.title: Be Attentive
items.body: When someone is talking, give them your full attention. Don’t busy yourself with something else; that’s just rude.

items.title: Be Bold
items.body: Life is an adventure. Don’t live it in fear. Pursue your dreams. Act on your instincts. Create the life you’ve always wanted.
items.related_read: How To Overcome Fear and Pursue Your Dreams

items.title: Be Candid
items.body: Be frank, outspoken, and earnest. Say what’s on your mind. Don’t feel the need to censor your words because you’re afraid of what others think. Be true to yourself. (But not at the expense of others’ feelings, of course. See #39: Be Empathetic.)

subitems.title: Show concern
subitems.body: There’s no need to wait for a cry for help before showing care and concern. You can do it right away, right now, to those around you. Even if there’s nothing wrong, it’ll warm the hearts of others to know that you care.

subitems.title: Call your friends
subitems.body: Are there any friends you’ve not contacted for a while? Call them today and check how they’re doing. They may not show it, but they’ll be happy that you called — because it shows that you care.

items.title: Be Coachable
items.body: There’s always something we can learn from everyone, no matter their age, background, or area of expertise. Don’t close off on opportunities to learn just because you think you know enough. Open your mind and let every encounter be a learning lesson. The moment you close yourself off is the point where you stop learning.

subitems.title: Find a mentor
subitems.body: A mentor guides you to become greater than you can be by yourself. Get a mentor if (a) the person has something to teach you and (b) your personalities gel with each other. Back when I was working at P&G, I had informal mentors who often stepped in to make sure I was doing well. At the same time, they had mentors who guided them. No matter how senior or experienced you may be, there is always someone with something to teach you.

items.title: Be Committed... to your goals and dreams
items.body: If you’ve set a goal, go all out and achieve it. If you’ve laid down a plan, stick to it all the way. Don’t waver, for that’s not in you to do so.

items.title: Be Compassionate / Kind
items.body: Always look out for opportunities where you can help others. Don’t get wrapped up in your stuff — instead, look outward and see if there’s anything you can do for others. Even the simplest things, like helping someone carry their belongings, are very much appreciated by others.

items.title: Be Confident... in who you are and what you do
items.body: There’s no reason not to be.
items.related_read: How To Be The Most Confident Person in the World

items.title: Be Conscientious / Meticulous
items.body: Are you attentive to everything you do? Such a quality is rare but so precious. Conscientious people put their heart and soul into what they do; consequently, they do a complete job in whatever they do. You’ll naturally be a valuable asset to whichever organization or team you’re a part of.

items.title: Be Considerate / Thoughtful
items.body: Make a habit to consider others in your decisions and actions for they affect other people. Make sure no one is negatively affected before you proceed with your plans.

subitems.title: Practice the Golden Rule
subitems.body: It’s the ethic of reciprocity which states “One should treat others as one would like others to treat oneself.” How do you want others to treat you? Shower others with this behavior and you’ll attract more of the same.

subitems.title: Practice the Silver Rule
subitems.body: Related to the Golden Rule, it states “Do not do unto others what you would not have them do unto you.” It’s to make up for the shortcomings of the Golden Rule. How do you not want others to treat you? Make sure you don’t do this to others.

items.title: Be Cooperative
items.body: Don’t be insular and seclusive. Be willing to work with others if they need your help. We don’t exist in this world alone; life is possible because we have each other.

items.title: Be Courteous
items.body: Practice good etiquette. Always remember your hi’s, bye’s, thank-you’s, and welcome’s.

items.title: Be Courageous / Overcome Fear
items.body: Is there anything you’re scared of? Don’t be. Fear is mental — It’s only what you perceive it to be. If you challenge the things you’re afraid of, you’ll realize there’s nothing to fear, because there is nothing to lose. We entered this world with nothing but our consciousness; we’ll leave the world with the same consciousness.
items.related_read: How To Overcome Fear and Pursue Your Dreams

subitems.title: Have an insatiable thirst for knowledge
subitems.body: So you’ll always be learning new things.

subitems.title: Ask questions — often
subitems.body: The more questions you ask, the more information you can uncover.

subitems.title: Get feedback from others
subitems.body: Feedback is one of the fastest ways to identify our areas of improvement since others can see our blind spots.

items.title: Be Dependable
items.body: Be there for others when they need you. Always check if there’s anything you can do for your friends. If they call you, make time out for them. If they email you, take the time to respond. You never know when it’s someone in pain and reaching out for help.
items.related_read: How to Have More Best Friends in Life

items.title: Be Discerning
items.body: Don’t blindly accept everything you hear or read; always evaluate what you’re given with a discerning mind. This doesn’t mean that you become skeptical, but that you exercise your judgment appropriately.

items.title: Be Emotionally Generous
items.body: Emotional stinginess means to be stingy with your emotions, while emotional generosity is to be generous. So, an emotionally stingy person is typically negative, unhappy, critical, judging, and imposing; while an emotionally generous person is positive, happy, encouraging, and supportive. Be as giving with your emotions as possible. Encourage others. Be positive. Share happiness.

subitems.title: Compliment others (with genuine intent)
subitems.body: Part of emotional generosity is to be generous with compliments (that are genuine and not fake). Get into the habit of giving compliments. When you meet someone and if you recognize something nice about them, let them know. You’ll make their day.

items.title: Be Empathetic
items.body: Empathy is the key to successful relationships. Learn to see things from others’ perspectives. It’ll let you understand people better, resolve conflicts, and develop meaningful connections.

items.title: Be Encouraging
items.body: No one likes a wet blanket. Be encouraging when your friends share their problems with you. Be supportive when they tell you about their goals.

items.title: Be Enthusiastic
items.body: Life is too beautiful to live with dread and boredom. Embrace every day with joy and love. Start every day on a fresh new start! Approach every situation with excitement! And bring this energy to everything you do and everyone you meet. :)

subitems.title: Take on more than you can handle
subitems.body: If you’re managing your responsibilities fine at the moment, challenge yourself by taking on more. It’s when you push your limits that you grow the most. Push your boundaries. Stretch yourself. This will increase your capacity as a person.

subitems.title: Expect nothing less than the best
subitems.body: Hold yourself to the highest standard in whatever you do. Always aim for the highest goals, the best results, and the grandest vision.

subitems.title: Live your life to the fullest
subitems.body: Because why should you settle for a life that’s anything less?
subitems.related_read: 101 Ways To Live Your Life To The Fullest

subitems.title: Don’t bad mouth other people
subitems.body: Don’t speak ill of people behind their backs, because it’s unfair to them and doesn’t give them a chance to defend themselves. Let the person know if you don’t like something he/she did, otherwise let it go.

subitems.title: Don’t discriminate
subitems.body: Give equal treatment to everyone, regardless of race, language, religion, nationality, gender, age, social status, and financial status.

subitems.title: Don’t judge
subitems.body: Don’t make conclusions about others’ character or their life based on 1-2 things you see about them. Always give others the benefit of the doubt.

subitems.title: Uphold justice
subitems.body: If you see unfairness being exacted, right the wrong. This includes intervening when someone is being bullied and standing up for someone when he/she is being unfairly judged.

items.title: Have Faith
items.body: Don’t put too much pressure on an event or a person to give you the results you seek. Do your best within your capacity and have faith that everything will fall into place.

items.title: Be Filial
items.body: Our parents dedicated half of their lives to having us and raising us. Now that we’re grown up, it’s our turn to repay them for the life they have given us. If your relationship with your parents is not the ideal state you envision, be sure to read How To Improve Your Relationship With Your Parents (series)

items.title: Be a Follower
items.body: Aristotle said it best with this quote: “He who cannot be a good follower cannot be a good leader.” Are you a good follower? Are you able to take directions from others? Are you willing to take directions from others? Before you think about becoming a leader (see #60), you’ve to learn to be a good follower first.

subitems.title: Let go of your anger
subitems.body: Is there anything or anyone you’re angry with? Perhaps it’s time to forgive and let things go.

subitems.title: Bury the hatchet with someone
subitems.body: Beyond embracing forgiveness within you, reach out to the person you had grievances with in the past. This is not going to be easy, but it’ll bring you a huge step forward in your growth. When I was younger, I had some conflicts with schoolmates due to misunderstandings. After I started PE, I decided I had to live by example if I was to pursue my purpose to help others how to achieve their highest potential. So I reconnected with old schoolmates whom I had conflicts with. It was much easier than I thought — most of them reciprocated in kind, and after that we stayed connected as friends.

items.title: Be Friendly / Approachable
items.body: We are all humans, here to connect. If you see someone you don’t know, take the first step to know them. With people you know, be accessible so they can approach you whenever they need help.

items.title: Be Generous
items.body: Find joy in giving. Life is not a zero-sum game. By giving, you get to gain even more. By giving, you open the channel to receive new things in life. When people experience the beauty of giving, they’d want to give back too, so what goes around, comes around.

subitems.title: Share the good things in your life
subitems.body: What are you happy about? What do you have that others don’t have? What are you proud of? Don’t keep them to yourself — Share them with others. Happiness isn’t a zero-sum equation.

subitems.title: Donate
subitems.body: Get in the habit of donating things you don’t need anymore. For example, old clothes, textbooks, books, toys, and the like. All my unwanted clothes are always donated to others. Sometimes I take the nice, unworn pieces and give them to my friends who can better appreciate them.

items.title: Be Gentle
items.body: Our society has brought out a very “hard” side in all of us — one where we’re abrasive, hard, and demanding. Bring out the gentle side in you for a change. It’ll make you a warmer person to be around.

items.title: Be Grateful
items.body: For the good things you have, because not everyone gets to have them. For the bad things you have too, because they strengthen your character and make you appreciate everything so much more.

subitems.title: Write a thank you note to a friend
subitems.body: I think a lot of times, we take our friends for granted. We forget about what they’ve done for us and are doing for us, as well as the value of our connection. Write a thank you letter/note/email to a friend and let them know how much you appreciate them. They will be very happy to receive your letter.

items.title: Be Hardworking / Diligent
items.body: Without hard work, we can’t get far in life. I’ve seen people who like to take the easy way out and this is not what I promote at PE. There are no “quick tips” or “hacks” that will give you instantaneous results — in the end, it’s about showing up and doing the work.

items.title: Be Helpful
items.body: Offer your help even if people don’t ask for it. There’s always something you can do for others.

items.title: Be Honest
items.body: To lie is to shrink into a lesser self; To tell the truth means to take a step up in your growth. (Unless there’s a higher value at stake, such as protecting someone’s well-being.) One of my values is truth: to discover the truth through personal experience and by constantly challenging what’s around me, and to be truthful in everything I do and say. I don’t achieve this 100% of the time, but I do my best to uphold it every moment of the day.
items.related_read: How To Deal With Dishonest People

items.title: Be Humble
items.body: Arrogant people suffer from an inferiority complex, which is why they feel the need to parade their accomplishments. Learn to be humble. There’s no need to repeatedly talk about what you’ve achieved just to assert your ability — when your work is good, the results will speak for themselves. (The exception is in professional contexts like on your resume or in interviews, where you are supposed to showcase your accomplishments.)
items.related_read: How To Keep Yourself Humble While Recognizing Your Worth

items.title: Be Independent
items.body: Learn to manage your life. Learn to tackle your problems by yourself, without imposing on others. Feel free to approach others if you need help, but you should never expect them to solve your problems for you.

items.title: Be Individualistic
items.body: Always be you. Don’t try to be anyone else.

items.title: Have Integrity
items.body: Set your moral and ethical principles and stick to them. Never compromise on them no matter what.

items.title: Be Intuitive
items.body: Follow your gut instinct. Let your intuition guide you. You’ll never go wrong with it. The more you follow your gut, the stronger your connection with your intuition will be.

items.title: Be a Leader
items.body: A leader is someone who brings the best out of others, who inspires others to be bigger than who they are, who energizes people into action, and who leads the way with a common vision. Contrary to what many think, leadership doesn’t begin when you lead a group of people. It begins in our everyday life, from how we conduct ourselves and live our lives. Are you a leader of your life?
items.related_read: You Are The CEO of Your Life

items.title: Be a Listener
items.body: The ability to listen is quite underrated in our society today. Many people are good at talking, but not listening. For today, make a point to listen to what others around you are saying. Ask questions. Clarify their answers. You may discover new things you didn’t know before.

items.title: Embrace Love
items.body: Be a beacon of love. Start by loving everyone around you. Show love to your friends, family, partner, colleagues, bosses, clients, teachers, etc. — whether explicitly or implicitly.

subitems.title: Love unconditionally
subitems.body: The highest form of love is unconditional love, where you love others without expecting anything in return.

items.title: Be Loyal / Faithful
items.body: To the people you care for, to the values you stand for, and to the things you believe in.

items.title: Be Kind
items.body: Don’t criticize. It’s easy to pinpoint faults in others, but really, it’s not in our place to do so. Not only that, it doesn’t make others feel good about themselves.

items.title: Be Magnanimous
items.body: For everything that people do you wrong, be ready to forgive and forget.

subitems.title: Accept criticism
subitems.body: If someone offers criticism, be ready to consider it. Considering it isn’t the same as agreeing. You don’t have to agree with the criticism, but at least consider it. Every criticism is an opportunity to improve, to become better.

subitems.title: Ignore malicious attacks
subitems.body: If someone flames you, take the higher route — ignore the person. You can defend yourself in areas where your values are infringed, but overall, keep a hands-off approach. It’s not worth it to engage in such discussions, because the flamer will only keep attacking with no desire to reach a resolution.
subitems.related_read: Empty Vessels Make the Most Noise

items.title: Be Meditative
items.body: Those who meditate will know that meditation cultivates inner peace within you. It makes you calmer and connects you with your inner self.
items.related_read: How To Meditate in 5 Simple Steps

items.title: Be Merciful
items.body: Instead of punishment, think forgiveness. Forceful actions like pain, suffering, and death don’t bring closure to issues.

items.title: Be Moral
items.body: Do what’s right over what’s wrong. The question of “what’s right” can be subjective depending on your upbringing, but universal values include equality of humans, gender equality, freedom of speech, and freedom of choice. Think about how you can follow a lifestyle that inflicts less pain on other living beings.

items.title: Be Mindful / Present
items.body: Don’t live in the past or future, but focus on the present moment. For this is where you’re living now. Meditating helps you to be present (see #66).

items.title: Be Nurturing
items.body: There’s always ability in everyone. How can you nurture it and bring it out of each person?

subitems.title: Recognize the strengths in others
subitems.body: Our society today has eased into a state where we keep looking at what we lack or don’t have, as opposed to what we already have. The former is a scarcity mindset, while the latter is one of abundance. Rather than think about what’s missing in someone (be it a character trait, knowledge, ability, or something else), focus on their strengths. What do they have? What are they good at? What do you like about them? Focus on these vs. what you don’t like.

items.title: Be Open-Minded
items.body: Be ready to accept different beliefs, attitudes, personalities, cultures, practices, rituals, lifestyles, habits, races, nationalities, diets, etc, for everyone is different. No one thing is right; it’s just a matter of what works best for the individual.

items.title: Be Optimistic / Positive
items.body: For life is too short to be negative.

subitems.title: Don’t complain
subitems.body: Complaining generates all this negative energy that makes you no different than an energy vampire. While it’s okay to vent occasionally, be conscious of the times when you do that. Cut down on the time you spend complaining and think about what you can do about the situation instead.

subitems.title: Smile
subitems.body: How often do you smile a day? Smiling is something we don’t do enough. Whether you’re out on the streets or at work, it’s more common to see people with stoic expressions and hard frowns than smiles. The next time you see someone, even a stranger, smile at them. You’ll be surprised how many people will return the smile. Even if they don’t, trust that they have been warmed by your smile.

subitems.title: Laugh
subitems.body: As they say, laughter is the best medicine. Learn to laugh at the jokes people make, at the obstacles you’re facing, at the mistakes you’re making, and at the mystery that is life.

items.title: Be Organized
items.body: The state of your life now reflects how organized you are. If everything is constantly in a mess, it suggests you’re probably disorganized in how you manage yourself. When you are organized, you create structure, stability, and predictability — which frees up your resources to pursue new goals. Creating a life handbook will help organize your life.

items.title: Be Patient
items.body: Do you get irritated when something/someone is late? Time is fluid; it’s a construct created to help us organize our schedules. Learn to be present and live in the moment instead. Impatience breeds anxiety; Patience brings calmness.
items.related_read: How To Be Patient: The Only Guide I’ll Ever Write on Becoming Patient

items.title: Be Peaceful
items.body: Where you have a choice, go for peace over violence. The latter solves nothing but creates more pain. The former is the start of a healing journey.

items.title: Be Persistent
items.body: No matter what you do, never give up. You will achieve whatever you set out to do, as long as you have the will to do it. My story of how I pursued my passion and turned it into a successful business is an example of that. The only time when giving up is the way to go is when your priorities change and you realize the goal you were pursuing isn’t what you want anymore.

items.title: Be Prudent
items.body: Be bold and daring, but at the same time exercise caution. A touch of practicality never hurt anyone; it helps you to be more ready for what’s ahead.

items.title: Be Purposeful
items.body: Pursue a cause that’s higher and larger than you. When you do that, you’ll naturally grow into someone bigger than who you are today. Pursuing my purpose to help others grow has made me embark on journeys and make decisions that I wouldn’t have pursued if I was just living my life for myself.
items.related_read: Discover Your Life Purpose in 30 Minutes

items.title: Be Reasonable
items.body: Know your rights, but don’t overstep your boundaries. Act within good reason — You’ll be the best judge of that.

items.title: Be Repentant
items.body: Has there been anything you did that you’re not too proud of? Repent and process it; don’t leave it inside your system, because it’s like rotting flesh — it’ll create an invisible stench and affect you subconsciously in your daily actions.

items.title: Be Resilient / Be Strong
items.body: Are you facing any obstacles that are making you waver in your goals? You have the strength inside you to do whatever you want — you just have to draw from it.
items.related_read: How To Start When You Have Nothing

items.title: Be Respectful
items.body: Treat everyone with the utmost respect, because every living being deserves that.

subitems.title: Live up to your responsibilities
subitems.body: What responsibilities do you have? Are you living up to all your responsibilities? Shrinking away from your tasks is an act of avoidance. Stepping up to them makes you a better person.

subitems.title: Don’t self-victimize
subitems.body: It’s easy to say, “Why me?” when bad things happen. But it does nothing to build your character — in fact, it makes you weaker over time because you’re not taking ownership of your problems. Believe it or not, everyone faces these problems too — it’s not exclusive to you. Rather than wallow in self-pity, accept your problems as part and parcel of life and address them. The more responsible you are, the more control you have over your life.

subitems.title: Be kind to yourself
subitems.body: Do you often beat yourself up? Stop doing that. You, above all else, deserve kindness and respect from yourself.

subitems.title: Love yourself
subitems.body: On a scale of 1-10, how much do you love yourself? The longest relationship you’ll ever be in is the one with yourself. When you improve your relationship with yourself, you’ll learn to be a better friend, partner, parent, and person.
subitems.related_read: What Can I Do If I Want To Change Someone?

items.title: Be Self-Reflective
items.body: I make a habit to reflect on everything that happens to me, because that’s when I can draw lessons on how I can do better in the future. Self-reflection can be done in a private journal or through conversations with others. Asking yourself the right questions is paramount in the self-reflection process.

items.title: Be Sensitive to others’ needs and feelings
items.body: Always check to make sure you’re not neglecting anyone.

subitems.title: Don’t Impose
subitems.body: Imposing means forcing your opinion on others. It’s okay to offer your opinion, but if others are not taking it, then there’s no need to repeat it. Keep it to yourself.

subitems.title: Don’t give unwanted advice
subitems.body: One of the biggest problems people face in relationships is when the other party tries to dispense advice that’s not needed. Many times, people converse as a way of sharing. Check if the other party is looking for advice first before you try to offer your 2 cents. It may help prevent unnecessary conflicts.

items.title: Dedicate yourself to service
items.body: It’s said that service to others is the highest thing one can ever do in life. Think about how you can contribute to others and this world. And dedicate yourself to it.

items.title: Be Sharp
items.body: Develop your observation skills. Sharp people are always the first to catch on to something, and because of that they’re ahead of everyone else.

items.title: Be Sincere / Genuine
items.body: Speak from the heart, always. Don’t say something unless you mean it. One of my core values is authenticity — I only say things that I mean, and never say things if I don’t believe in them.

items.title: Be Spontaneous
items.body: Be uninhibited! Allow yourself to act freely, without restrictions. Not everything has to adhere to a plan all the time. Allow yourself to just go with the flow. :D

items.title: Be Sympathetic
items.body: If others are sharing their problems with you, be sympathetic. Don’t jab in with insensitive remarks. Don’t dismiss their feelings and thoughts. Get yourself into the same state as them and express your sympathy, so they know they’re not alone in the situation.

items.title: Be Tactful
items.body: There’s no need to be rude or abrasive. Be polite to your fellow humans — everyone has feelings, even if sometimes it may not seem that way.

items.title: Be a Teacher
items.body: You don’t have to be a teacher by title. The very act of sharing knowledge with someone is teaching in itself. By teaching others, we become better. What are things that you’re good at? Share the knowledge with other people. Start by doing it informally, and soon formally teaching others will be second nature to you.

items.title: Be Trusting
items.body: Always give others the benefit of the doubt. No matter what you think, the baseline intention of people is usually good. No one deliberately does something to harm others. When they do, it usually comes from a place of lack, not out of sheer malicious intent. At the same time, don’t let others take advantage of you.
items.related_read: How To Be a Good Friend Without Others Taking Advantage of You

items.title: Be Trustworthy
items.body: Always honor your commitments and uphold your promises. If you make an agreement with someone, be sure to stick to it.

items.title: Be Unattached
items.body: For all things are transient in life. This doesn’t mean you become jaded and an emotionless being. What this means is you relish in every moment of your life, every situation you’re in, every person you’re with, as it is, without clinging on to it when it has passed. For we live in the present, not the past or future.

items.title: Be Understanding
items.body: Learn to comprehend things from others’ perspectives. You need a common understanding to build relationships.

items.title: Be Vigilant
items.body: While the world is a safe place by and large, keep a watch out for possible dangers, especially when you’re in a foreign place. Keep a look out for suspicious people. Stay clear of potentially dangerous spots. It’s better to be safe than sorry.

items.title: Be Visionary
items.body: Set the highest goals and the biggest dreams you can imagine! Then set off and bring your vision to life. Create your vision board too. Here’s my video on Creating Your Vision Board.

items.title: Be Vulnerable
items.body: Through PE, I’ve learned that sharing our vulnerabilities is what gives us the greatest strength as humans. In the past few years, I’ve opened up about some of my deepest vulnerabilities, including my relationship with my parents, my past heartbreak, my disappointments, and my emotional eating issues.

items.title: Be Wise
items.body: Being wise means “having the power of discerning and judging properly as to what is true or right; possessing discernment, judgment, or discretion.” Practice good judgment by exposing yourself to different contexts; considering different perspectives; gathering as much information as you can; weighing out different possibilities. The more experience you gain, the more you learn, and the wiser you’ll become.
